key_insight: Among five HVOF-sprayed cermet coatings on 65G steel, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall balance of densest microstructure, highest hardness, and lowest friction.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical machine components, the WC–Co–Cr system appears to be the strongest candidate when both abrasive-adhesive resistance and coating integrity matter.
method: HVOF-sprayed WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr onto 65G steel.
Compared microstructure by SEM/EDS, plus microhardness, roughness, tribology, and adhesive strength.
Compared performance across coating composition and binder phase effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports measured differences in friction (μ = 0.143–0.630), microhardness (631.59–1316.87 HV), roughness (Ra = 3.881–8.130 μm), and scratch/adhesion behavior across the coatings.
watch_item: Results are coating-system specific and depend on spraying conditions, so transfer to other substrates or HVOF parameter sets should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
